subject.title: [Bug]: Clarify Telegram channel_post auth when groups[chatId].allowFrom is configured

question: For Telegram `channel_post` native/plugin commands, should `groups[chatId].allowFrom` be ignored in favor of explicit chat allow, or should sender-scoped `allowFrom` make `channel_post` commands unsupported/fail-closed?
rationale: Either choice defines a command-authorization boundary on a Telegram surface where normal human sender identity is unavailable, and repository policy treats fallback/security-boundary choices as maintainer-owned product decisions.

options.title: Fail Closed For Sender-Scoped Overrides
options.body: Reject `channel_post` commands when sender-scoped per-chat `allowFrom` is configured, with clear messaging and docs explaining that Telegram does not expose the required human sender identity.

options.title: Use Explicit Chat Allow Only
options.body: Permit commands from explicitly configured channel chats and document that per-chat sender-scoped `allowFrom` is ignored on this surface.

options.title: Defer To Bot-To-Bot Policy Work
options.body: Keep this open until broader Telegram bot-to-bot policy work defines channel, peer, sender, and loop-guard semantics together.

recommendation.title: Fail Closed For Sender-Scoped Overrides
recommendation.body: Reject `channel_post` commands when sender-scoped per-chat `allowFrom` is configured, with clear messaging and docs explaining that Telegram does not expose the required human sender identity.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest recent history in Telegram native command and callback behavior affected by this decision.
